presentation: A 58-year-old woman with a 6-month history of progressive proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash on the eyelids, and Gottron papules over the MCP joints. CK elevated to 4200 U/L. ANA positive.
reasoning: Classic triad of proximal weakness + heliotrope rash + Gottron papules with elevated CK is pathognomonic for dermatomyositis.

presentation: A 24-year-old man with sudden-onset bilateral vision loss, urinary retention, and lower-extremity weakness over 3 days. MRI shows longitudinal extensive transverse myelitis spanning T4-T10 plus optic nerve enhancement.
reasoning: Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis combined with optic neuritis is the hallmark of NMOSD.

presentation: A 45-year-old construction worker with progressive dyspnea, dry cough, finger clubbing over 18 months. HRCT: peripheral, basal-predominant reticular opacities with honeycombing.
reasoning: UIP pattern on HRCT (basal-predominant reticular + honeycombing) in older patient without secondary cause is IPF.

presentation: A 67-year-old man with isolated diastolic dysfunction, low-voltage ECG, monoclonal gammopathy on SPEP, and bilateral carpal tunnel history.
reasoning: Low-voltage ECG despite LV hypertrophy + monoclonal protein + carpal tunnel triad strongly suggests AL amyloid.

presentation: A 32-year-old woman with episodic palpitations, headache, and diaphoresis, with paroxysmal hypertensive episodes to 220/130. Plasma metanephrines elevated 10-fold.
reasoning: Classic triad (palpitations, headache, sweating) with paroxysmal HTN and dramatically elevated metanephrines is pheo until proven otherwise.
